scripts.short_description: Show the <title> of the home page on each HTTP/HTTPS service
scripts.long_description: Connects to detected web servers and reports the page title — a quick way to see what's running. Pulled in automatically when you select 'default scripts'.

scripts.short_description: List HTTP response headers (Server, X-Powered-By, etc.)
scripts.long_description: Useful for fingerprinting the web stack: which server software, which framework, any obvious version disclosure.
Collects the host key types and fingerprints. Handy for inventorying SSH servers or detecting key changes (man-in-the-middle indicator).

args.name: ssh_hostkey
args.description: Output format: hex, full, sha1, sha256, mr (machine-readable)

scripts.short_description: List authentication methods accepted by an SSH server
scripts.long_description: Tells you whether the server allows password auth, publickey, keyboard-interactive, etc. — useful when planning credentialed access without actually attempting login.

scripts.short_description: Identify the OS of an SMB server (Windows version, domain, NetBIOS)
scripts.long_description: Talks SMB to the host and surfaces the OS, computer name, NetBIOS name, domain or workgroup, and system time. Often the fastest way to find Windows boxes on a LAN.

scripts.short_description: List the SMB dialects a host supports (SMB1/2/3)
scripts.long_description: Useful for detecting hosts still speaking deprecated SMB1 — a frequent finding in enterprise environments and a known security risk.

scripts.short_description: Retrieve TLS/SSL certificate details (CN, SANs, issuer, expiry)
scripts.long_description: Dumps the X.509 certificate served on each TLS port: subject, subject alternative names, issuer, validity dates, signature algorithm. Great for spotting expiring certs or wildcards.

scripts.short_description: Enumerate the TLS cipher suites accepted by a server, with strength grades
scripts.long_description: Negotiates handshakes against the server to enumerate supported protocols, ciphers, and elliptic curves. Outputs a quality grade for each. Slower than ssl-cert.

scripts.short_description: Look up CVEs for detected service versions in the Vulners database
scripts.long_description: Reads the version detected by -sV and queries vulners.com for known CVEs. Output includes CVE IDs, CVSS scores, and links — a great first pass at vuln assessment.

warnings.text: Sends queries to api.vulners.com. Don't run on air-gapped or sensitive networks where outbound traffic is restricted.

scripts.short_description: Check whether the FTP server allows anonymous login
scripts.long_description: Attempts an anonymous login and lists the root directory if successful. Common finding on misconfigured legacy FTP servers.
Triggers the smiley-face backdoor in vsftpd 2.3.4 to confirm vulnerability. Actually attempts the exploit — the script opens a shell on port 6200 if successful.

warnings.text: Intrusive — actually attempts the exploit. Only run against systems you own or have explicit authorization to test.

scripts.short_description: MySQL server version, capabilities, and connection salt
scripts.long_description: Connects to the MySQL handshake (no login) and surfaces the protocol version, server version string, supported capabilities, and the auth-plugin name. Non-intrusive.

scripts.short_description: Brute-force common DNS subdomains against a domain
scripts.long_description: Queries a wordlist of typical subdomain names against the target's authoritative DNS. Useful for asset discovery; can be noisy and DNS providers may rate-limit.

warnings.text: Generates many DNS queries. Use only against domains you own or that explicitly permit it.

args.name: dns-brute.hostlist
args.description: Path to a custom subdomain wordlist

args.name: dns-brute.domain
args.description: Domain to brute (defaults to the target)

scripts.short_description: Grab the welcome banner emitted by open ports (FTP, telnet, SMTP, etc.)
scripts.long_description: Reads the first response chunk from each open port. Cheap and harmless; useful when -sV is overkill.

scripts.short_description: WHOIS lookup for the target's domain (registration data)
scripts.long_description: Performs a WHOIS query to retrieve domain registration metadata. Talks to external WHOIS servers — same caveat as vulners.

warnings.text: Sends queries to external WHOIS servers; not appropriate for air-gapped environments.
